sections.body: Seaweed grows under light, temperature, salinity, current, and other environmental conditions suited to the species. Unfed aquaculture still requires stock preparation and deployment, density management, and checks of lines and fouling organisms. Excessive density may affect light and water flow, but adjustments follow the plan rather than one universal number. Record and report color changes or tissue damage. Adapt harvesting, drying, or storage to the product and prevent contamination from equipment and the work area.

sections.body: Handle aquaculture products using containers, water, ice, and areas suitable for each product. Keep clean routes separate from waste, chemicals, and contaminated equipment. Cooling and other processes must meet the commodity's needs; live stock, fresh fish, shellfish, and seaweed may require different handling. Do not use one temperature or method for everything. Time and condition records support assessment when deviations occur. Separate questionable lots so decisions are not based only on odor or color.

sections.body: Unit reports include species or lot, time, water parameters, actual feed, mortality, transfers, and approved actions. 給餌量 means “feed amount,” and 水温 means “water temperature.” Unclear units can change a decision; ask for repetition and confirm figures before acting. Distinguish measured data from estimates. The official aquaculture examination is in Japanese, while this material provides an Indonesian bridge through vocabulary and cases. Reading comprehension does not replace training in measurement, equipment, or water-work safety.
